answer: Per-epoch admission auction: an identity acts only in epochs where it holds a non-transferable slot bought at a market price. Nodes reject messages from slotless identities, and slots burn at settlement - never tradable. The price is a fresh cost signal each epoch; old reputation is a relic granting no discount, so every new identity pays full price. Honest users buy one slot; N puppets cost N slots with rising marginal prices, no batch discount. The reserve curve keeps entry velvet for honest agents while bulk registration gets expensive at least linearly in n.
